locator.name: the last line is shortened to 300 characters

proves.facet: A last line longer than 300 characters is cut to 300 in the wake.

locator.name: a line for a parent in a turn waits for that turn and is not sent into it (MIK-R172@v2 rule 6)

proves.facet: A recipient in a turn is not steered into; the line is held and goes when that turn ends.

locator.name: a refused return gives the line (MIK-R172 rule 4)

proves.facet: A `role_message` call answered as refused does not count as a return, so the line goes out.

locator.name: a parent whose provider is unknown is treated as one that does not steer

proves.facet: An absent provider reads as unknown, and unknown holds.

locator.name: turn-end order survives an in-flight prior flush (L172-R4-F02, schedule one)

proves.facet: A later flush waits for the one in flight, so an earlier line is never overtaken.

locator.name: held lines are sent in the order the turns ended, across a requeue (rule 6)

proves.facet: Three lines held for one running parent are delivered together, in the order their turns ended, once that turn ends. The test's own failed-send call is never reached because the parent is still in its turn, so it exercises held order, not a requeue.

locator.name: a second batch is not sent into the parent turn the first batch started (L172-R4-F01)

proves.facet: The gate is asked again at each actual send, and the unsent tail stays owed.

locator.name: provider history is reclaimed on archive and capped (L172-R4-F03)

proves.facet: Archive reclaims the provider entry and the history keeps its named bound.

locator.name: a silent end sends one line with the facts and the agent's last line

proves.facet: A silent end's single line names the role, agent, task and newest report and carries that turn's last line.

locator.name: an empty last text says no text and an unreadable one says so

proves.facet: An empty turn says `no text` and an unreadable timeline says `unreadable`, and neither suppresses the line.

locator.name: a parent whose provider is known to steer gets the line at once (MIK-R172@v2 rule 6)

proves.facet: Named steering knowledge is the only case in which a mid-turn recipient takes the line immediately.

locator.name: turn-end order survives Manager rebinding (L172-R4-F02, schedule two)

proves.facet: Rebinding to the current Manager keeps the order the turns ended in.

locator.name: an agent whose recorded parent is archived wakes the current Manager of its master

proves.facet: An archived parent's ended turn wakes the current Manager of the same master.

locator.name: a real failed send keeps the debt and is retried in order, once (L172-R4-F02 retry)

proves.facet: A throwing sender leaves the debt owed and the retry delivers it once, in order.

locator.name: a held line reaches the successor when the archive has no alternate yet (L172-R1-F02)

proves.facet: With no alternate recorded at archive time the line stays owed and reaches the successor exactly once.

locator.name: an empty ended turn says no text, never an earlier turn's text (L172-R1-F01)

proves.facet: An ended turn with no text of its own reports `no text` instead of repeating an earlier turn's line.

locator.name: an agent the agent list does not hold is named in the host log once

proves.facet: An agent outside the product's list yields no line and one host-log entry, not silence.

locator.name: a return in an earlier turn does not silence this turn's line (L172-R1-F01)

proves.facet: An accepted return in an earlier turn does not suppress the ended turn's line.

1.note:
The host-free suite retains suppression/deferral/retry/restart controls and adds actual parent-wake registration against a mock registry with explicit steer sends.
